title: Divide a String Into Groups of Size k
statement:
Cut the string `s` into consecutive pieces of exactly `k` characters, reading from left to right, so that every character of `s` lands in exactly one piece. If the final piece comes up short, pad its end with copies of the character `fill` until it reaches length `k`. Return the list of pieces in order.

Joining the pieces and then dropping the padding from the last one gives back `s`.
constraints: s contains only lowercase English letters
fill is one lowercase English letter
signature: String[] divideString(String s, int k, char fill)
notes:
## Intuition

The pieces are fixed by position: the first starts at index 0, the next at index `k`, then `2k`, and so on. Only the last piece can be shorter than `k`, and topping it up with `fill` is all the extra work there is. There are `ceil(n / k)` pieces in total.

## Approach

1. Start with an empty list `groups`.
2. Move `start` through `0, k, 2k, ...` while it is still inside `s`.
3. Take `group` as the characters from `start` up to (not including) `start + k`; `slice` simply stops at the end of the string.
4. While `group` is shorter than `k`, append `fill`. This only happens for the last piece.
5. Push `group` and continue; finally return `groups`.

## Example 1, step by step

`s = "abcdefghi"`, `k = 3`, `fill = "x"`.

- `start = 0`: `group = "abc"`, already length 3, push it.
- `start = 3`: `group = "def"`, push it.
- `start = 6`: `group = "ghi"`, push it.
- `start = 9` is not below 9, so the loop ends and the answer is `["abc","def","ghi"]`.

In Example 2 the extra `start = 9` gives `group = "j"`, which is padded twice to `"jxx"`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(n + k): every character of `s` is copied once, and at most `k - 1` fill characters are added.
- Space: O(n + k) for the returned pieces.

## Pitfalls

- Stepping `start` by 1 instead of by `k` produces overlapping pieces.
- Padding every piece instead of only the short one: full pieces must stay untouched.
- When `k` is larger than `s.length` the answer is a single padded piece, not an empty list.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `groups` | the pieces built so far |
| `start` | index in `s` where the current piece begins |
| `group` | the current piece, padded with `fill` if needed |

narration.2: Collect the pieces in this list.
narration.3: Each piece begins k characters after the previous one, until start runs past the end of s.
narration.4: Take up to k characters starting at start; slice stops early at the end of the string.
narration.5: A piece shorter than k can only be the last one, so it needs padding.
narration.6: Append one fill character and check the length again.
narration.8: Store the finished piece of exactly k characters.
narration.10: Every character has been placed; return the pieces in order.
